data: Test your knowledge of the 2026 FIFA World Cup — the first to feature 48 teams across the United States, Canada, and Mexico.
How many teams participated in the 2026 FIFA World Cup, marking the first expansion to this format?
The 2026 World Cup expanded to 48 teams, up from the 32-team format used since 1998.
Which three countries co-hosted the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
The United States, Canada, and Mexico co-hosted the 2026 World Cup — the first tournament with three host nations.
Which stadium hosted the 2026 FIFA World Cup Final?
MetLife Stadium in New Jersey hosted the 2026 World Cup Final.
Which historic venue hosted matches at both the 1970 and 2026 FIFA World Cups?
Estadio Azteca in Mexico City hosted games in 1970, 1986, and again in 2026, making it the only stadium to host matches at three World Cups.
In the new 48-team group stage format, how many teams advanced from each group of three?
All three plus best third-place sides
The 2026 World Cup used 16 groups of three teams, with the top two from each group advancing to a 32-team knockout round.
Which confederation qualified the most teams for the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
UEFA received 16 spots in the expanded 48-team tournament, the largest allocation of any confederation.
Roughly how many cities across the three host nations staged 2026 World Cup matches?
The tournament spanned 16 host cities: 11 in the United States, 2 in Canada, and 3 in Mexico.
Which Canadian city hosted group-stage matches at the 2026 FIFA World Cup?
Both Toronto (BMO Field) and Vancouver (BC Place) hosted 2026 World Cup group-stage matches for Canada.
